title: ErrorPage
summary: A whole screen that failed (not found, forbidden, server error, offline or maintenance): MonarchErrorState at the large size, centered on the canvas color.
whenToUse: As the content of a screen the app navigated to that cannot be shown at all: a record that does not exist, no access, the service down, no connection.
whenNotToUse: When only part of a screen failed, use MonarchErrorState in that region or MonarchInlineErrorRetry. For a failure the user can fix in a form, use field errors.
api: Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize().background(MonarchTheme.colors.bgCanvas), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) { MonarchErrorState(title, kind = MonarchErrorStateKind.NotFound, size = MonarchEmptyStateSize.Lg, message = …, requestId = …, onRetry = …, actions = { … }) }

options.name: kind
options.description: NotFound, Forbidden, Server, Offline or Maintenance; sets the default wording of the state.

options.name: title
options.description: What happened, in plain words, supplied by the app.

options.name: message
options.description: What the person can do next. Never a raw error.

options.name: requestId
options.description: The id of the failed request, for support.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: A retry button, for Server, Offline and Maintenance.

options.name: actions
options.description: The app's way out, such as "Go to projects".

states.name: not found, forbidden
states.description: The title, message and a way out; no retry.

states.name: server, offline, maintenance
states.description: The same with a retry button; retrying shows the button as busy.

appearance: MonarchErrorState at its large size, centered on the canvas background color that fills the screen. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ErrorPage is a component with a large faint numeral (404, 403, 500), an optional brand, a support slot and a retry when the browser comes back online, and it can render without the app shell. On Android a destination that fails is a screen inside the app's navigation, so the recipe fills it with MonarchErrorState; the numeral is left out because it means little in an app, and the title says what happened. To retry when the network returns, register a ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback in the app and call the same retry. focusOnMount has no equivalent: TalkBack reads the new screen from the top. iOS shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: MonarchErrorState marks its title as a heading and reads the message after it.
Retry and the actions are buttons with 48dp touch targets.
The screen keeps the app's top app bar, so back and navigation still work.
edgeCases: Use fillMaxSize inside a scrolling container only with a bounded height; the catalogue uses fillMaxWidth.
Offline: do not retry in a loop; retry once when the connection returns.
